moat_against: Clover competition from Toast and Block is structural
Pricing power eroding — fee concessions and margin compression
Large clients can renegotiate, in-source or leave at renewal
Management credibility: repeated guidance resets, CEO turnover, Clover litigation, activist pressure
moat_for: Core processing embedded in 10,000+ FIs — high switching costs, long contracts
Scale in merchant acquiring; Clover leading SMB POS position, GPV +9% in Q2 2026
Net debt only 0.12x normalized OE; buybacks shrinking share count 5.4%/yr
moat_justification: Core bank/payment processing is mission-critical infrastructure embedded in 10,000+ financial institutions with high switching costs, long contracts and 84% recurring revenue, and Clover holds a leading small-merchant POS position with GPV still growing — but Clover competition from Toast/Block is structural, pricing power is visibly eroding (fee concessions, adjusted operating margin down to 31.8% from 39.6%), Financial Solutions is shrinking, and repeated guidance resets plus CEO turnover show the moat did not protect growth or margins. Moderate-strong, not wide: 6/10, CAP 9.8 years.
name: Fiserv, Inc.
one_liner: High-quality cash machine (TTM OE $6.64/sh, 14.4% OE yield, net debt 0.12x OE) with a moderate-strong 6/10 moat, priced for failure after two years of guidance resets — clears 15% on recalibrated, bear-skewed inputs (weighted IRR 18.0%, weighted IV@15% $57.66 vs $46.19 price; $57.66 is the highest price clearing 15%), but only the super-bear case is insured against.
